intent.instructions: What does `request` ask the assistant to do about meetings? Ignore unrelated chatter around it.

criteria.book_one: it asks to schedule exactly one meeting now
criteria.book_several: it asks to schedule two or more meetings or sessions
criteria.not_booking: it asks about a meeting, asks only for options without booking, says to wait, or asks to cancel, move, hold or draft, or asks for something that is not scheduling

outsider.instructions: Does `request` name anyone to attend the meeting who is neither in `known_people` (full or first name) nor the user `user`?

extra.instructions: Does `request` put any condition on the meeting other than who attends, how long it lasts, which weekdays of this week are allowed, an earliest start time and a latest end time? Examples: a room, an exact fixed start time, a recurring series, another week, a vague part of day.

length.instructions: How long, in minutes, should the meeting requested in `request` last?

criteria.other: a length is stated but it is not one of the listed values

bound.instructions: Which time-of-day limit does `request` put on the meeting it asks for?

criteria.end_by: only a latest time by which the meeting must be finished
criteria.start_from: only an earliest time at or after which the meeting must start
criteria.both: both an earliest start time and a latest end time
criteria.none: no time-of-day limit at all
criteria.other: some other kind of time limit, such as an exact start time or a vague part of the day

title_first.instructions: Which word of `request` is the first word of the name of the meeting to book (for example the 'hiring' of 'hiring debrief')? Do not count articles, lengths or people.
